excerpt: Bitcoin fell to nearly $60,000 yesterday. This was the worst single-day drawdown since the FTX collapse in 2022.

spans.text: Bitcoin fell to nearly $60,000 yesterday. This was the worst single-day drawdown since the FTX collapse in 2022.
But today the market is breathing again: we are close to reclaiming the $70,000 level after forming a bottom.
It may be the formation of the first higher high since $90k. If the week closes above $68k, it confirms support at the
A retest of the $74k to $79k region would be natural, even if more declines happen afterward.
Yesterday’s drop was expected, but its speed was a bit scary. What happens next, no one knows. But you can prepare for some scenarios:

items.text: From now on, the chances of falling another 50% are lower than the chances of rising 50%. The asymmetry is very favorable.
Cycle bottom regions are between $58k and $42k. This may generate more fear and better buying opportunities.
If the price keeps rising, we should find resistance starting around $75k.
Thinking about a new ATH now is crazy. We are very far from it and still need to break above the 100- and 50-week moving averages before considering a return to a bull market.

spans.text: For those who want to analyze it more deeply:

items.text: NUPL entering capitulation zone: This means most investors are in the red and starting to sell in panic. Historically, this marks market bottoms.
SOPR below 1: confirms that Bitcoin holders are selling at a loss.
Exchange reserves rising: selling pressure on Bitcoin.
Negative funding rates: this means the market is pessimistic and more people are shorting (betting against) than buying.

spans.text: All these signals together show extreme fear in the market. It looks bad, but historically this is when bottoms are formed.
Some of what is happening in the world and affecting asset prices, including Bitcoin:

items.text: Increasing correlation with the struggling software/tech sector
Traders betting that the Fed will keep rates unchanged in April
Layoffs in the U.S. at the highest level in 17 years, which may pressure the Fed to cut rates sooner (bullish in the medium term)
